summary: Customer wants to use an in-line UV-Vis fiber probe to continuously measure viable cell concentration in a stirred mammalian cell bioreactor culture medium, and asks whether this would work in their medium.

facts_stated.text: Growth occurs in a stirred bioreactor.
The customer has a culture medium.
The customer currently takes manual samples for cell counting.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: taking manual samples for cell counting

process.enquiry_quote: taking manual samples for cell counting

customer_premises.claim: A UV-Vis fiber probe can measure viable cell concentration continuously.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: want a UV-Vis fiber probe to measure the viable cell concentration continuously

customer_premises.claim: The proposed UV-Vis measurement will work in the customer's culture medium.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: Would this work in our culture medium?

customer_premises.claim: The probe can replace manual samples for cell counting.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: so we can stop taking manual samples for cell counting

unknowns: optical properties of the medium (scattering, absorption, turbidity)
temperature and pressure at the measurement point
pH, dissolved oxygen, and dissolved CO2
presence of bubbles, particles, or microcarriers
installation point and distance (in situ, bypass, probe length)
required accuracy, precision, and response time
limit of detection and dynamic range
ability to distinguish viable from non-viable cells
